analysis.investment_thesis: Kaveri Seed is a genuinely good business — debt-free, ~20% ROIC, 48% gross margins — but at an earnings yield of only ~6.2% (EBIT INR 291 Cr / EV ~INR 4,693 Cr), it falls well short of the Magic Formula's attractiveness threshold of 12%+. The quality is there; the bargain is not.
key_strengths: Virtually zero debt (borrowings = INR 0 Cr in 2025) with INR 1,785 Cr reserves — fortress balance sheet
ROIC ~20% (ROCE 20.1%) with 48% gross margins, reflecting genuine seed genetics IP and pricing power
OCF positive all 5 years (INR 108–389 Cr range), proving earnings quality despite lumpiness
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 5.5% over 9 years — a high-ROIC business that can't grow is worth far less to a Magic Formula screen
FCF is lumpy and falling: INR 289 Cr in FY24 collapsed to INR 108 Cr in FY25 as capex remains elevated (INR 89–110 Cr/yr)
Seed business is highly weather/monsoon-dependent; FY22 net profit crashed to INR 213 Cr from INR 311 Cr — cyclicality is real
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~6.2% is barely above the Magic Formula's minimum — not a bargain
Other income (INR 46 Cr in FY25) is a meaningful 16% of net profit — strip it out and core earnings look weaker
CWIP of INR 100–134 Cr suggests ongoing capacity expansion but revenue growth hasn't kept pace
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on KSCL: EBIT of INR 291 Cr against an Enterprise Value of ~INR 4,693 Cr (market cap INR 4,713 Cr minus cash INR 20 Cr, zero debt) gives an earnings yield of 6.2%. That's barely above the floor — Magic Formula demands 12%+ to rank attractively, and 15%+ to get genuinely excited. On the quality side, ROIC proxied by ROCE at 20.1% is decent but not exceptional (I want 25%+). The business earns above its cost of capital, but not by a wide enough margin to compensate for the mediocre cheapness score. EV/EBITDA of 12x and P/E of 15.8x confirm the market is already pricing in quality.

The business fundamentals are admirable: zero debt, consistent profitability across a decade, high gross margins from proprietary hybrid seed genetics, and strong promoter commitment at 60.5%. But the Magic Formula is a dual-filter system — you need BOTH cheapness AND quality. KSCL passes on quality and fails on cheapness. Worse, revenue growth at 5.5% CAGR over 9 years means there's no growth engine to eventually justify paying up. I'd want to see the stock at 40–50% lower prices (implying earnings yield of ~10%+) before this enters the buy zone.
